title: Decode Ways
description: A message of capital letters is encoded as digits using `A = 1, B = 2, ..., Z = 26`. Given a digit string `s`, return how many different ways it can be decoded back into letters. A code with a leading zero such as `"06"` is not valid (it is not the same as `"6"`), and `0` alone maps to no letter.

examples.explanation: A leading zero cannot be decoded.

constraints: s contains only digits and may start with 0
hints: Look at the end of the string: the last character may be one code, or the last two may form a code.
Let dp[i] be the number of ways to decode the first i characters. When is it valid to extend from dp[i-1]? From dp[i-2]?
A single digit is valid if it is 1-9; a pair is valid if it lies in 10-26. Only the last two dp values are needed.

solution.explanation: Let dp[i] count decodings of the first i characters. A nonzero last digit lets you extend dp[i-1], and a last two-digit number between 10 and 26 lets you add dp[i-2]. Zeros that cannot pair with a preceding 1 or 2 give zero ways. Only two previous values are kept, so O(n) time and O(1) space; plain recursion repeats subproblems exponentially.
